newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent gains 10 cents but further selling seen.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent gains 10 cents but further selling seen.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures made 10 cents a barrel gains as the NYMEX market moved nervously higher in early trade, but the gains were not expected to last with technicals further selling pressure to come, traders said.
"API days are usually reversible off the implied move," said Charles Gray analyst at Prudential-Bache International Ltd.
He said several technical factors continued to indicate room for "a bit more downside" with five and 15 day moving averages crossing over indicating a sell signal.
By 1538 GMT the February Brent contract was trading 15 cents a barrel firmer at $23.51 cents a barrel.
Feb gas oil was $2 a tonne firmer at $215.75 a tonne. Here again Gray said the market still had downside potential but much would depend on the performance of NYMEX heating oil.
Brokers attributed earlier gains in both complexes to better-than-expected American Petroleum Institute (API) oil stock data.
API data showed the shortfall in gasoline inventories widened to 9.35 million barrels against year-ago levels from the 6.5 million barrels figure reported last week.
Distillates registered a 1.29 million fall on the week, including a 419,000 barrel fall in the key northeast coast PADD 1 district.
Brokers said that while the data bode well for product futures, relatively milder weather in Europe has dampened its effect on gas oil.
